summary: Return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1.
mainInsight: Naive matching re-compares characters; a rolling hash lets you test each window in O(1) before a real comparison, and KMP guarantees O(n + m) by never moving backwards in the haystack.

approaches.name: Rolling hash (Rabin-Karp)

approaches.name: KMP

personalSolution.notes: Correct because of the verification step. A polynomial rolling hash or KMP gives better guarantees; in practice use str.find.

promptVariants: Why must a rolling hash match be verified with a real comparison, and why is a sum of ord() values a weak hash?
Why is a plain sum of character codes a poor rolling hash and why must matches still be verified?
cards.answer: Different windows can share the same hash (collisions); equality of hashes only suggests a match. Sum of character codes ignores order, so every anagram of the needle collides, making verification (and the worst case) frequent. A polynomial hash (Rabin-Karp) is far less collision-prone.
cards.explanation: Verification keeps the result correct even with collisions.

promptVariants: Worst-case time of KMP: ___ (n = haystack, m = needle)

cards.explanation: Preprocessing O(m) plus a single O(n) scan.

promptVariants: Compare the space of naive search, rolling hash and KMP.
What does KMP cost in memory compared with the naive and rolling-hash methods?
cards.answer: Naive and rolling hash: O(1). KMP: O(m) for the prefix table. KMP buys worst-case time with that memory.

promptVariants: Why is the window hash updated with `- ord(haystack[i]) + ord(haystack[i + m])` and why is the update guarded by `i < n - m`?
Explain how the window hash is updated in O(1) and why the last update is skipped.
cards.answer: Sliding by one removes the character leaving the window and adds the one entering, so each hash costs O(1). The guard stops the update after the last window, where haystack[i + m] would be out of range.
keyPoints: Guard avoids index out of range
cards.explanation: Worst case O(n*m) because the hash collides on anagrams of the needle.
